subject: Privacy confirmation & next steps — prompt/response storage and deletion
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Walker <lauren@healthcorps.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2029 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: HealthCorps integration — privacy & prompt outputs (post-demo recap)

Hi Lauren — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap (and answers) from our side so your security and privacy team has a clear view of what we store, where, and how long. Attaching a short PDF + a retention matrix for reference.

Summary of what we store by default (configurable per customer):
- Prompt text: stored by default to support debugging, evals, and quality improvements.
- Generated output: stored by default for observability and post-hoc review.
- Request metadata: timestamps, model id, latency, approximate token counts; no automated extraction of user PII beyond what exists in the payload.

Where stored / residency options:
- Hosted default: US-West (AWS us-west-2).
- EU option: can be pinned to eu-central-1 for EU-only residency (adds a regional routing policy).
- Private / Dedicated: deployable into customer VPC or on-prem with full data residency control.

Encryption & keys:
- At-rest: AES-256. By default we manage keys.
- Customer-managed keys: supported via AWS KMS (BYOK) for Hosted + Dedicated.
- In transit: TLS1.3.

Retention & deletion options (configurable):
- Ephemeral mode: do not persist prompts or outputs (inference handled in-memory, no logs retained).
- Short TTL (default for trials): prompts & outputs persisted for 30 days then compacted; debugging logs persisted 90 days unless disabled.
- Custom TTL: customers can set 0/7/30/90/365 days.
- Deletion API: immediate deletion is available via API (DELETE /v1/outputs/{id}) and bulk requests via our data-deletion endpoint.

Logging & access control:
- Audit logs: admin-level access logs retained for 365 days (can be extended with an add-on).
- Role-based access: granular RBAC in Console; token-level tracing can be disabled.

Redaction & PII handling:
- Automated redaction: optional regex-based redaction for structured fields (SSNs, credit cards) at ingress.
- Manual redaction: admin UI and API for one-off removal.
- Field-level scoping: you can route only non-PII fields into the model and keep raw payloads out of storage.

Next steps we propose:
1) Share HealthCorps’ data classification table (sample attached) so we can mark the proper fields for automated redaction.
2) Security questionnaire (we’ll fill in SOC2 / KMS details) — we’ll return the completed PDF by EOD tomorrow.
3) If you want BYOK, we’ll schedule a short setup call with infra (SojiN) to bind your key and test a churn cycle.

Attachments: redwood_pii_handling_summary.pdf (TL;DR), redwood_prompt_retention_matrix.xlsx (TTL options + defaults)

Open to any clarifying questions — I / Soojin / Marissa are on copy.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Lauren Walker <lauren@healthcorps.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: security@healthcorps.ai, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2029 16:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthCorps integration — privacy & prompt outputs (post-demo recap)

Thanks Jonas, this is very helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security team: 

1) For the default "stored" mode — can you confirm whether stored outputs are encrypted with a unique per-customer key (i.e. envelope encryption) or a shared tenant key?
2) If we choose "ephemeral mode" (no persistence), is there any possibility of caching in the serving layer that might persist data beyond the request window? If so, what is the max cache window?
3) We also need an SLA for deletion requests as part of our procurement — what is Redwood's target TTR for API deletion calls and for bulk manual deletion requests?
4) For EU residency option: does routing to eu-central-1 guarantee that copies (backups, logs) will not leave EU for any maintenance operations?

Appreciate a concise confirmation we can share with procurement/security. If useful, can Soojin respond with the technical details and any API examples.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Walker
Head of Product, HealthCorps
lauren@healthcorps.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Walker <lauren@healthcorps.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2029 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthCorps integration — privacy & prompt outputs (technical confirmation)

Hi Lauren — quick technical confirmations below so you can forward to procurement/security. Happy to hop on a call if you want to walk through keys and API flows.

1) Encryption model:
- We use envelope encryption. Each customer in Hosted gets a unique data-encryption key (DEK) that is encrypted with a master key. BYOK: you may supply a CMK via AWS KMS; we support binding your CMK so DEKs are wrapped with your key.

2) Serving cache behavior in ephemeral mode:
- Serving runtime keeps a short-lived KV cache for KV-cache acceleration (to support streaming / long-context reuse).
- Max cache TTL in ephemeral/no-persist mode is 60 seconds by default and can be set to 0 (disabled) for strict non-persistence.
- No persistent write-to-disk occurs in ephemeral mode.

3) Deletion SLA:
- API deletion (single id): best-effort under 60s; background purge processes may take up to 24 hours to fully remove from all indexes and backends.
- Bulk deletion / legal requests: standard target TTR is 72 hours; we offer expedited 24-hour handling for enterprise / signed SOWs.

4) EU residency guarantees:
- When you pin to eu-central-1 we ensure primary data, backups, and standard logs remain in EU regions. We do not replicate primary storage to non-EU locations unless you enable multi-region failover.
- For maintenance we perform remote admin actions from our control plane; for customers requiring strict EU-only admin operations we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/private control plane) or Dedicated with EU-only operator agreements.

5) Audit & access logging:
- Admin audit logs (console/API auth events) default retention 365 days in region; all accesses are scoped by RBAC.
- Access to raw prompt/output blobs by Redwood support/engineers requires an approved internal request and is logged (and you can require a manual approval workflow).

6) API examples (snippet):
- Single delete: DELETE https://api.redwood.com/v1/outputs/{output_id} (Authorization: Bearer ...)
- Bulk delete job: POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/data-deletion-requests {"filter": {"account_id":"HC-XXXX","older_than_days":30}}

7) Additional controls:
- Field-level redaction hooks (ingest webhooks) so you never send PII to the model.
- Pre-signed retention windows and auto-expiry policies configurable per route.

If you want, we can produce a short one-page attestation you can include in procurement. Also attaching a small sample curl collection and the retention matrix.

Cheers,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Security & Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
